questions.explanation: An action completed before another past action → past perfect.

questions.q: Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.explanation: "be going to" for predictions based on present evidence.

questions.q: I ___ my homework yet.
While we ___ dinner, the phone rang.
questions.explanation: A longer action in progress interrupted by a short one → past continuous.

questions.q: By next June, I ___ from school.
Water ___ at 100 °C.
They ___ for two hours when the bus finally came.
questions.explanation: Duration of an action up to a point in the past → past perfect continuous.

questions.q: How long ___ English?
questions.explanation: "How long" + an action continuing until now → present perfect continuous.

questions.q: I ___ Salalah three times this year.
questions.explanation: "this year" is an unfinished time period → present perfect.

questions.q: This time tomorrow, I ___ on the beach.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time → future continuous.

questions.q: If you heat ice, it ___.
questions.explanation: Zero conditional (general truth): If + present, present.

questions.q: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present, will + verb.

questions.q: If I ___ rich, I would travel around the world.
questions.explanation: Second conditional (unreal present): If + past simple ("were" for all subjects).

questions.q: If she had studied harder, she ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.q: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
I would call him if I ___ his number.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: would + verb … if + past simple.

questions.q: "If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have missed the flight." This is the ___ conditional.
questions.explanation: Past perfect + would have + past participle = third conditional.

questions.q: ___ I you, I would apologise.
questions.explanation: Inversion of the second conditional: "Were I you" = "If I were you".

questions.q: If he ___ the alarm, he wouldn't have been late.
You can borrow my car ___ you drive carefully.

units.title: الوحدة الثانية: المبني للمجهول والكلام المنقول (Passive & Reported Speech)

questions.q: The letter ___ yesterday.
questions.explanation: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle.

questions.q: English ___ in many countries.
questions.explanation: Present simple passive: am/is/are + past participle.

questions.q: The new bridge ___ at the moment.
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: am/is/are + being + past participle.

questions.q: The results ___ next week.
questions.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.q: The homework ___ already ___.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have + been + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the passive form of: "They clean the classroom every day."
options: The classroom is cleaned every day.
The classroom was cleaned every day.
The classroom is cleaning every day.
questions.explanation: Present simple active → present simple passive.

questions.q: Choose the passive form of: "Someone stole my bike."
questions.explanation: Past simple → was + past participle. "by someone" is usually omitted.

questions.q: The work must ___ before Friday.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle.

questions.q: We usually use the passive when ___.
options: the doer of the action is unknown or unimportant
we want to emphasise who did the action
we talk about the future only
questions.explanation: The passive focuses on the action or the thing affected, not the doer.

questions.q: The book was written ___ a famous Omani author.
questions.explanation: "by" introduces the doer (agent) in a passive sentence.

questions.q: He said, "I am tired." → He said that he ___ tired.
questions.explanation: Present simple → past simple when reporting.

questions.q: She said, "I will come tomorrow." → She said she ___ come ___.
"Where do you live?" he asked. → He asked me ___.
questions.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order and no question mark.

questions.q: "Did you finish the report?" she asked. → She asked ___ I had finished the report.
questions.explanation: Yes/No questions are reported with "if" or "whether".

questions.q: The teacher said, "Open your books." → The teacher told us ___ our books.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + infinitive.

questions.q: "Don't be late," he said to me. → He told me ___ late.
questions.explanation: Negative commands: tell + object + not to + infinitive.

questions.q: "I have lost my keys," Ali said. → Ali said he ___ his keys.
In reported speech, "here" usually changes to ___.
questions.explanation: Place words shift: here → there, this → that.

questions.q: "We can swim," they said. → They said they ___ swim.
"I saw him yesterday," she said. → She said she ___ him ___.
questions.explanation: Past simple → past perfect, "yesterday" → "the day before".
